description_full: Chery Automobile Co., Ltd. designs, develops, manufactures, and sells passenger vehicles, and automotive parts and components in the People's Republic of China and internationally. It offers internal combustion engines and new energy vehicles, and KD kits. The company also provides after-sales services. It offers its products under the CHERY, JETOUR, EXEED, iCAR, LEPAS, and LUXEED brand names. The company was incorporated in 1997 and is headquartered in Wuhu, the People's Republic of China.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 70K people. Revenue per employee of $644K ranks in the above the sector median among Consumer Cyclical peers. Each employee generates $11K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $1K per employee reflects an ownership culture. CEO compensation is 1× revenue per employee (modest relative to workforce productivity). R&D investment of 4% of revenue (limited) signals commitment to product development and talent.
financial_summary: Chery Automobile Co., Ltd. is a large-cap consumer cyclical business with a $16.4B market cap on $45.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +45% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.

Returns on capital run at 93% against a 9% cost of capital — a 83-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 14% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $790M in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.06× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 7.3×.

Net dilution runs at 5.1% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 69% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
